The implementation is complete and validated. Summary of what I built:

## Changes to the supplied NetNomos core

**`netnomos/theory.py`** â added `compile_term` / `compile_formula`: a vectorised compiler that turns the NetNomos formula AST (built from the protocol JSON by the supplied `ast.py` + `projection.py` projector) into a closure `f(matrix) -> bool ndarray`, so the identical predicate object evaluates training windows and every universe window. Made the pandas import lazy (the exact engine never materialises a dataframe).

**`netnomos/learners/hittingset.py`** â added the exact discovery core (`others_mask`, `is_inclusion_minimal`, `enumerate_minimal_clauses`): a DFS over strictly increasing predicate ids that emits *exactly* the inclusion-minimal covering clauses. Key insights used: clauses covering all training windows are hitting sets of the per-window evidence sets; any strict superset of a covering set is never minimal, so a branch stops at the first covering prefix; a literal that adds no fresh coverage can be pruned. Universe truth masks are carried for the conditionâ3 filter. Two subtle bugs were caught and fixed during validation: masks must be sized by explicit window counts (a falsified final window clears the top bit), and "literal *i* is essential" needs the OR of the **other** literals, not `covered & ~literal_i`.

**`netnomos/finite.py`** â the exact protocol pipeline: `WindowSchema` (layout, AST predicates, ids preserved) â `WindowUniverse` (mixed-radix enumeration, index 0 = all-smallest, slot-major/field-order, domain *positions* as digits) â `ClauseMiner` (all eligible clauses + per-literal witness = lowest training index where that literal is the only true one, counterexample = lowest universe index falsifying the clause, sorted by `(length, ids)`) â `active_theory` (approved â© discovered, in rule order) â `decode_queries` (joint theory â§ fixed bindings â§ canonical-decimal prefix match; `count` counts windows, `witness` is the smallest index, tokens `"0".."9"` then `"END"`).

## Validation
- `python3 public_check.py submission` â **PASS**.
- Two *independent* reference implementations (pure-Python brute force, and a numpy combination-enumerating reference) agree with the engine on ~2500 random protocol-valid jobs plus targeted edge cases (universe size 1, tautologies, always-false literals, constant-only comparisons, duplicate rows, 1000000-valued domains, sums/scales, `any`/`all` with K=4, leading-zero and 7-digit prefixes).
- 4500+ randomized mask-level trials of the enumerator vs. brute-force minimal-transversal enumeration.
- Prefix matcher checked exhaustively (0..19999) and on 4000+ boundary/random values over `[0,1000000]`; universe ordering/indexing verified on 1820 random layouts.
- In-spec worst case (2Ã65536 universe, 32 predicates, 10000 train windows, 256 approvals, 256 queries) runs in ~2 s wall under the exact `limits.py` child policy; submission is 15 entries / 68 KB.
